executiveSummary: GM0489 passes the deterministic national contract over all ten canonical scenarios, T+0/6/12/24/48/72 and all eight essential services. Official 2025 identity and headline demography, 62 neighbourhoods, one BAG place, four BRT settlements, five A15/A29 logical routes, null handling, service-specific local allocation, arithmetic, causal ledgers, exact zero-intensity behavior and sustained-water recovery guards are coherent. Release remains correction-required for two local spatial blockers. First, generic centre-to-line river/coastal functions produce municipality-wide exact inundation stress without naming a failed defence, connected hydraulic footprint or event scenario: river T+24 emits 2.640520 internal stress, 29,739 people under pressure and zero recovery, while coastal T+24 emits 1.104884, 26,249 people and zero recovery. Barendrecht's adopted strategy instead distinguishes the primary/secondary dikes and compartments protecting IJsselmonde from the Oude Maas, a small raised outer-dike strip and mechanism-specific breach consequences. Second, all three water mechanisms receive the same deterministic neighbourhood rank. Documented 2018/stress-test hotspots include Paddewei, Meerwede, Oranjewijk, Centrum and the Oude Dorpskern/Zeeheldenbuurt, yet Paddewei ranks 61st of 62 for pluvial stress while uncalibrated Vrijenburg ranks first. The adopted urban-water programme and public Waterschapshuis objects provide stronger non-causal context, but do not supply hydraulic connectivity or live state. Barendrecht is in Stedin territory while the current utility-context UI is Liander-only. All eight intermunicipal flows correctly remain logical transfer proxies; missing or security-sensitive utility topology, capacities, backups, stocks, crews and restoration estimates were not invented.

evidenceSources.title: Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025 — filtered municipality row GM0489
supports: Official-context GM0489/Barendrecht identity, population 48,550 and density 2,480 residents per square kilometre.
Official age-65-plus count 9,738, equivalent to the generated rounded share 20.1%, and 5,369 one-person households.
The OData table is machine-readable, updated annually and published under CC BY 4.0; rounded and suppressed neighbourhood values require explicit reconciliation/null semantics rather than imputation.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek
evidenceSources.title: Gemeente gegeneraliseerd 2025
supports: Official annual CC BY 4.0 generalized GM0489 polygon consumed by the application.
Municipality-centre point-in-polygon validation and the polygon used for neighbourhood/public-asset intersection checks.
The generalized CBS administrative geometry is a distinct product from BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlement objects and must not be treated as a hydraulic boundary.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Rotterdam-Rijnmond 2026–2029, versie 1.0
supports: Official regional-context evidence listing Barendrecht and ranking extreme rain, failure of primary/regional barriers, electricity, telecom, cyber, industrial hazardous-material and transport disruption among material regional risks.

The profile distinguishes binnendijk flooding after barrier failure from smaller regional-water mechanisms, and says stormwater systems can process approximately 20 mm per hour while heavier rain may remain on the surface.

It supports dependency directions from electricity into drinking water, wastewater, health, mobility and telecom, and describes emergency drinking-water planning above 24 hours; it does not publish local operator topology, outage probabilities, asset state, resources or restoration forecasts.

This is an official strategic/consultation scenario source, not an observed/live feed or machine-readable local hazard footprint. Final post-consultation adoption was not independently established during this audit; no fixed refresh cadence or explicit document reuse licence was stated.

evidenceSources.title: Strategie klimaatadaptatie Barendrecht 2022–2026
supports: Official local context distinguishes primary and secondary protection of IJsselmonde, the Noldijk/Ziedewijdsedijk/Achterzeedijk/Koedood line, Bakkersdijk and Middeldijk compartments, and a small generally raised unprotected outer-dike strip along the Oude Maas.

The strategy reports 50–70 mm of rain in a short period on 29 May 2018 and identifies Oude Dorpskern/Zeeheldenbuurt, Centrum, Oranjewijk, Meerwede and Paddewei among water-nuisance/stress-test locations.
It documents heat hotspots and vulnerable older residents and links to municipal climate-stress-test maps.

This is adopted policy plus historical/contextual evidence, not a live observation service, reusable machine GIS export or calibrated depth/arrival product; no explicit dataset licence or fixed machine-update cadence was verified.

evidenceSources.title: Programma Stedelijk Water 2024–2028
supports: Official local inventory reports approximately 337 km gravity sewer, 61 km mechanical sewer, 54 sewer pumps, four surface-water pumps, one drainage pump, twelve tunnel pumps and 201 pressure-sewer pumps.

Almost all wastewater and stormwater systems are separated; roughly 5 km of mixed sewer remains around Smitshoek and Stationsweg, with a named overflow/storage arrangement, and wastewater is treated at Barendrecht and Zwijndrecht.

The programme uses GWSW data management, says pumps are continuously monitored, sensor quality is reviewed monthly and performance is reported annually, and identifies heavy-rain inflow issues at Drechtwaard.

The official publication is policy/inventory evidence, not a public operational API or complete licensed topology. Its programme edition is 2024–2028; no general reuse licence for live municipal telemetry was exposed.

evidenceSources.title: Uitbreiding elektriciteitsnet in Barendrecht and Stedin open liggingsdata
evidenceSources.edition: current project page and Stedin annual open-data documentation inspected 2026-09-02
supports: The municipality identifies Stedin as the grid operator and states that local low-voltage expansion began in Nieuweland at the end of 2024 and is planned across neighbourhoods and business areas through 2030.

Stedin publishes integration-ready downloadable SHP geometry for cables, pipes and stations at https://www.stedin.net/zakelijk/open-data/liggingsdata-kabels-en-leidingen in RD New coordinates, with a snapshot date and at least annual refresh after each calendar year.

The public files exclude service connections, public lighting, assets not owned by Stedin and assets no longer in use; they are static context, not current state, switching, capacity, backup or KLIC replacement.

Stedin states the files may be used freely, but this audit did not find a named standard open-data licence on the download documentation; licence terms must be recorded and cleared before redistribution.

evidenceSources.title: Nationaal Wegenbestand Wegen OGC API
supports: Machine-readable road-section geometry underlying Barendrecht's five corrected A15/A29 cross-boundary logical routes.
The national source is continuously maintained, released monthly and published under CC0.
NWB supplies static road geometry and identity, not live closure, congestion, evacuation throughput, repair access or utility-network capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards via PDOK
evidenceSources.title: Waterschappen Kunstwerken IMWA and Waterketen DAMO OGC APIs
supports: Machine-readable object-level official context; the current generalized-boundary intersection contains 118 objects: 81 weirs, 35 surface-water pumps, one sewer pump named Barendrecht Drechtwaard and wastewater treatment Barendrecht.
Kunstwerken IMWA is CC BY-SA 4.0; its current landing metadata did not expose a fixed updateFrequency, so feature timestamps and retrieval time must be retained.

The companion Waterketen DAMO API at https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-waterketen-damo/ogc/v1 is also CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness and no fixed cadence exposed on the current landing page.

The single public sewer-pump object cannot be reconciled as a complete inventory against E05's differently scoped 54 sewer pumps and 201 pressure-sewer pumps; neither API establishes controls, connectivity, emergency power, live state or restoration time.

notes: The corrected routes are A15 to Rotterdam, Ridderkerk and Albrandswaard and A29 to Hoeksche Waard and Rotterdam; all municipality endpoints resolve.

emergencyContext.summary: Authoritative sources establish locally specific flood, drainage, heat, infrastructure and cascading-failure context that the generic first-72-hour model only partially represents.
notes: E04 distinguishes primary/secondary dikes, compartments, protected binnendijk areas and a small outer-dike strip, and identifies named observed/stress-test pluvial hotspots.
E05 documents a large mostly separated sewer system, named pump/tunnel assets, Drechtwaard inflow issues and operational monitoring practices.
E03 supports extreme rain, barrier failure, electricity, telecom, cyber, industrial and transport cascades but supplies no municipality event probability or operator capacity.
The public context layer exposes 118 intersecting water objects with official-context, partial and affectsSimulation=false semantics.
No sensitive utility topology, live incident/asset state, crew, fuel, priority-customer list, facility capacity, stock or operator restoration commitment was inferred.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets completed at T+0, 6, 12, 24, 48 and 72 for all eight services.
notes: Peak municipality severities were storm 0.596725, pluvial 0.719337, river 0.833853, coastal 0.287783, heat 0.756786, winter 0.618195, cyber 0.577924, earthquake 0.006042, wildfire 0.105418 and compound 0.983278.

At T+24 compound had rain 57.570532 mm/h, inundation-stress amplitude 0.793065, wind 28.044999 m/s, cyber disruption 0.507012, system pressure 0.628601, 33,421 people under pressure and 552,580 cumulative event-attributable essential-service person-hours.

At T+72 compound retained severity 0.656401, inundation-stress amplitude 0.793065 and cyber disruption 0.065942, with pressure 0.612446, 32,316 people under pressure and 2,030,307 cumulative proxy person-hours.

apps/web/src/scenarios.ts clones the canonical sim-core presets, so the audited configurations match user-selectable scenarios. All output values are deterministic derived scenario estimates, not observations, forecasts or incident reports.

numericalInvariants.summary: Finite bounds, exact no-event semantics, determinism, monotonic cumulative burden, route bounds and municipality/local reconciliation pass.
notes: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0489 pnpm audit:model passed both tests across 10 presets × 6 checkpoints × 8 services in 27.15 seconds.
Every canonical preset with intensity zero produced exactly zero current severity, peak severity, affected population and event-attributable essential-service person-hours at every checkpoint.
Repeated T+24 frames were byte-deterministic; all state remained finite/bounded; cumulative person-hours were monotonic; route flow never exceeded effective logical capacity.
Compound T+24 local allocation reconciled population 48,550, affected population 33,421 and demand/delivery for all eight services, with maximum numerical discrepancy below 2.5e-14.
The zero-resident business neighbourhood Vaanpark 2 receives service-specific non-residential demand without inventing residents, and changing among all 11 map layers leaves physical state invariant.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Generic municipality-wide water forcing and identical seeded neighbourhood ranks do not represent Barendrecht's defences, compartments, outer-dike strip or documented rain hotspots.
notes: River inundation stress rises from 0 at T+0 to 0.929463 at T+6 and 2.640520 at T+12, then stays 2.640520 through T+72; affected population rises from 10,702 at T+6 to 29,739 at T+24 and 30,731 at T+48/T+72.
Coastal T+6/12/24 reports inundation-stress amplitude 1.104884 and wind 20.097681 m/s, with 26,249 people under pressure at T+24; forcing clears by T+48 but generic recovery remains slow.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-475 derives river/coastal exposure from municipality-centre distance to coarse reference lines; lines 589-604 apply preset amplitude without selecting a named breach, defence state, outer-dike polygon, compartment, depth, arrival or duration product.

packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3323-3337 multiplies municipality severity by 0.82–1.18 using hazardSeed for every neighbourhood. Pluvial, river and coastal therefore have the same exact ranking: Vrijenburg first and Paddewei 61st of 62.

At pluvial T+24 Vrijenburg receives local hazard severity 0.654167 while Paddewei receives 0.463466, despite E04 naming Paddewei—and also Meerwede, Oranjewijk, Centrum and Oude Dorpskern/Zeeheldenbuurt—as observed/stress-test water-overlast locations.
The result is deterministic but not hydraulic evidence; CBS boundary/density, a seed and public point assets cannot establish direct water footprints.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight service balances are inspectable, but their first-72-hour values are not calibrated to Barendrecht's public assets or physical provider networks.
notes: River T+24 availability was power 0.455819, water 0.349031, drainage 0.324858, gas 0.664570, telecom 0.379870, mobility 0.566951, facilities 0.520189 and supply 0.154853.
Compound T+24 availability was power 0.514559, water 0.273146, drainage 0.313300, gas 0.554747, telecom 0.205054, mobility 0.698333, facilities 0.260151 and supply 0.149899.
E03 supports dependency direction and E05 supports actual sewer/pump context, but neither calibrates these exact modeled availability, demand, delivery or repair values.

The causal graph has no explicit Noldijk/Middeldijk compartment, municipal pump/tunnel node, Drechtwaard inflow, wastewater-treatment dependency, Stedin asset, drinking-water pressure zone, telecom site, care role or supply-stock node.
All eight service views reuse the same five A15/A29 corridors and nominal sum 1,300; every edge correctly declares transferSemantics logical-proxy.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, service and municipality ledgers close and preserve scenario confidence, dependency ordering, controls and counterfactual scope.
notes: Hazard contributions sum to headline severity; each service baseline plus contribution deltas sums to availability; all eight weighted service-pressure contributions sum to municipality system pressure.
Dependency chains, driver metadata, local vulnerability/demand factors, recovery progress and service-restoration counterfactual deltas are finite and arithmetically closed.
Household preparedness affects modeled population/supply burden after physical pressure and does not change physical hazard fragility.
Operational controls and time-gated interventions are labeled scenario assumptions, while common road-derived utility corridors remain logical transfer proxies.
Event-attributable essential-service person-hours integrate weighted unmet-service pressure as a planning approximation, not observed customer outage-hours, casualties, displacement or welfare loss.

recovery72h.summary: Sustained-water and response-delay guards operate consistently, but unsupported footprints and absent local resource/state data prevent operational recovery interpretation.
notes: River water remains active at T+72, all eight service recovery-progress values remain exactly zero, pressure is 0.589283, 30,731 people remain under pressure and cumulative proxy burden reaches 1,754,515 person-hours.
River T+72 keeps seven service availabilities at their T+24 values while facilities falls from 0.520189 to 0.416530 through generic dependencies; this is not an operator/facility forecast.
Coastal direct forcing clears by T+48; pressure falls from 0.523738 at T+24 to 0.237058 at T+72, affected population from 26,249 to 6,639, and service recovery progress spans 0.479079–0.939839.

Ended storm, pluvial, winter, wildfire and earthquake forcing recovers monotonically; heat/drought and cyber retain bounded forcing under their preset schedules; compound residual water prevents a generic all-clear.
Actual defence/control state, pump operation, utility switching, roads, crews, mutual aid, fuel, spares, staff, stock and restoration estimates remain unknown.

findings.summary: River and coastal presets create exact municipality-wide inundation without selecting a Barendrecht defence failure or connected hydraulic footprint.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 establish real flood relevance but distinguish primary/regional barrier failure, binnendijk compartments and a small raised outer-dike Oude Maas strip. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:430-475 and 589-604 instead use municipality-centre proximity to coarse river/coast reference lines. River produces internal inundation stress 2.640520 at T+12 through T+72, pressure 0.574771, 29,739 people and 459,251 cumulative event-attributable service person-hours at T+24, then 30,731 people and 1,754,515 person-hours at T+72. Coastal produces stress 1.104884, pressure 0.523738, 26,249 people and 397,971 person-hours at T+24. No named breach, barrier condition, defence compartment, outer-dike mask, depth, arrival, duration or uncertainty supports those exact footprints or exposed populations. This is municipality-specific evidence of a shared national proximity-field defect, not a claim that Barendrecht has no flood risk.
findings.action: Until a selected authoritative hydraulic scenario exists, do not present exact direct water, affected population or no-recovery consequences as municipality evidence; expose the direct footprint as unknown or require an explicit synthetic breach/outer-dike scenario. Durable correction must intersect a named/versioned LIWO or water-board depth/arrival/duration footprint with GM0489, preserve dike/compartment/outer-dike semantics and keep river, coastal, regional-barrier and pluvial mechanisms separate.

findings.summary: The mechanism-invariant seeded neighbourhood rank contradicts documented Barendrecht rain-hotspot evidence.
findings.evidence: E04 reports the 29 May 2018 50–70 mm cloudburst and names Oude Dorpskern/Zeeheldenbuurt, Centrum, Oranjewijk, Meerwede and Paddewei among observed/stress-test problem areas; E05 adds real sewer/pump and Drechtwaard evidence. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:3323-3337 instead assigns severity × (0.82 + hazardSeed × 0.36). The exact neighbourhood ordering is identical for pluvial, river and coastal hazards: Vrijenburg is first and Paddewei 61st of 62. At pluvial T+24 Vrijenburg is 0.654167, Sint Clarabos 0.651078 and Voordijk 0.637251, while Paddewei is 0.463466 and Buitenoord 1 is 0.456737. No terrain, drainage catchment, street-depression, sewer, pump, barrier or calibrated stress-test cell causes that ordering.
findings.action: Replace the hash as the primary direct-water allocator with versioned intersected local stress-test/hydraulic geometry. Use AHN terrain and public water/sewer assets only as disclosed covariates—not depth results—and retain unknown/no-data. Add fixtures that named source hotspots/footprints control local rank and that pluvial, river and coastal mechanisms can produce different spatial ordering.

findings.summary: Barendrecht's documented drainage/wastewater system is absent from causal pluvial response and the public object layer is not a complete inventory.
findings.evidence: E05 reports 337 km gravity sewer, 61 km mechanical sewer, 54 sewer pumps, four surface-water pumps, one drainage pump, twelve tunnel pumps and 201 pressure-sewer pumps, along with Drechtwaard heavy-rain inflow. E08 yields 118 public context objects but only one DAMO sewer pump and one wastewater-treatment object; their collection correctly says partial and affectsSimulation=false. Pluvial T+24 drainage availability is therefore a generic modeled balance rather than a consequence of a named catchment, pump, sewer mode, storage basin, emergency power or monitored state.
findings.action: Ingest GWSW/DAMO/IMWA and a licensed municipal export as non-causal context with explicit scope first. Connect a named asset or catchment only when the municipality/water board supplies approved topology, control logic, capacity and backup; otherwise retain a bounded service-specific scenario fallback and never infer completeness or operation from public point presence.

findings.summary: Barendrecht is served by Stedin, but the current power/gas evidence overlay and inspector expose only Liander coverage.
findings.evidence: E06 identifies Stedin and its Barendrecht reinforcement programme and publishes annual downloadable cable/pipe/station geometry. apps/web/src/data.ts:506-560 loads a partial Liander context source only, while apps/web/src/components/Inspector.tsx:258-263 presents that Liander evidence row for power/gas. Thus absence of a local utility feature is a provider-coverage gap, not evidence of no asset. The simulation itself does not consume the Liander layer, so numerical behavior is unchanged.
findings.action: Add a provider-aware Stedin context adapter with source snapshot date, exclusions, licence status, affectsSimulation=false and coverage polygons; show ‘not covered by this provider dataset’ rather than an empty Liander result. Do not infer current state, capacity, switching, fragility or restoration from static geometry, and require licence clearance before redistributing cached files.

findings.summary: Every essential service reuses five road corridors rather than Barendrecht-specific utility, care or supply topology.
findings.evidence: Power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply expose the same five A15/A29 edges to Rotterdam, Ridderkerk, Albrandswaard and Hoeksche Waard with nominal capacity sum 1,300. E07 supports static road geometry only; E03 supports cascade direction, not those service topologies or capacities. packages/sim-core/src/model.ts:1955-1986 and every emitted route correctly label the transferSemantics as logical-proxy, preventing a physical cable/pipe claim.
findings.action: Retain the explicit fidelity disclosure. Add independent public context per service where licensed, but promote a route to physical only with provider-approved topology, direction, capacity, backup and current state. Otherwise keep distinct inspectable service-specific synthetic/logical graphs rather than implying that road capacity is cable, pipe, telecom, patient-transfer or food capacity.

findings.summary: Static A15/A29, station and GTFS context does not establish first-72-hour emergency mobility.
findings.evidence: The bundle contains five valid NWB routes, Barendrecht station and 61 GTFS stop areas, but mobility T+24 is derived as 0.566951 in river and 0.698333 in compound without dated closures, congestion, tunnel/bridge state, rail operations, vehicles, evacuation demand or emergency access. E07 explicitly supplies geometry rather than live capacity.
findings.action: Retain NWB monthly CC0 geometry; integrate timestamped NDW DATEX II speeds/intensities/incidents/closures/works from https://opendata.ndw.nu/ (typically minute-scale feeds; record the exact feed licence and validity) and editioned ProRail CC0 geometry as separate observed/context inputs. Keep rail operation, evacuation capacity and response access unknown without live/authorized data.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter and cyber values are synthetic scenario stressors rather than dated Barendrecht observations, warnings or incidents.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 support regional/local relevance of severe weather, heat, drought, cyber and infrastructure cascades. The model peaks—storm 0.596725, heat 0.756786, winter 0.618195 and cyber 0.577924—derive from canonical schedules and deterministic seeds. At T+72 heat retains drought 0.639487/current severity 0.115108 and cyber retains disruption 0.057792. No KNMI station/grid time, warning validity, measured local heat exposure, named cyber target, provider incident or observed outage supports the precise values.
findings.action: Keep scenario/evidence confidence prominent. Optionally ingest timestamped KNMI open observations/grids/warnings with their product resolution, validity, update interval and licence, and accept only authorized incident targets for cyber exercises; never label a canonical preset as forecast, probability or live outage.

findings.summary: Remote Groningen-earthquake and wildfire presets remain bounded screening cases rather than Barendrecht risk assessments.
findings.evidence: Earthquake peaks at severity 0.006042, has zero current shaking and zero affected population at T+24, and accumulates 6,525 proxy person-hours by T+72. The remote wildfire has zero direct flame at T+24, smoke 0.218978, drought 0.513520, severity 0.105418 and zero affected population, accumulating 168,739 proxy person-hours by T+72. E03 describes no active local fault scenario; neither preset supplies event probability, local ground motion/site response, fuels, ignition, smoke dispersion, access or suppression state.
findings.action: Retain explicit remote-event naming and separate direct versus indirect effects. Require event-specific KNMI ground motion and validated local fragility for an earthquake, or an explicit fire origin/perimeter plus authoritative land cover and weather for a local wildfire; do not interpret small/zero direct forcing as a universal all-clear.

findings.summary: Official identity, rounded demography, null handling, settlement semantics and service-specific local allocation are inspectably coherent.
findings.evidence: E01/E02 agree with GM0489 identity and headline totals. All 62 neighbourhoods preserve unavailable values as null; rounded local population differs by only five; one BAG place centre is inside; BAG/BRT/CBS semantics stay separate; and compound T+24 local population, affected people, demand and delivery reconcile municipality values across all services. Zero-resident Vaanpark 2 receives transparent non-residential service demand without inventing residents or measured critical load.
findings.action: Retain source editions, null semantics, distinct geography products, vulnerability-context disclosures, service-specific non-residential allocation and exact reconciliation tests.

findings.summary: The deterministic, causal, zero-intensity, sustained-water and UI semantic contracts pass for GM0489.
findings.evidence: The focused gate passed ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services; zero intensity exactly clears severity/peak/affected/person-hours; T+24 repeats exactly; numerical/route bounds hold; all ledgers and counterfactuals close; and sustained water blocks elapsed-time restoration. A headless Chromium check selected Barendrecht, coastal surge and T+24, exercised all 11 map layers, displayed normalized ‘inundation stress’, 26.2K people under pressure, official water assets and the fidelity text ‘Official geography, transport & public assets · logical service transfers · scenario impacts’, and produced no page, console or failed-local-response errors.
findings.action: Preserve these national invariants while correcting GM0489-FLOOD-001 and GM0489-PLUVIAL-SPAT-001; add exact Barendrecht source-footprint and provider-coverage fixtures without weakening no-event, layer invariance or causal reconciliation.

corrections.summary: Require a named, connected hydraulic scenario for Barendrecht river/coastal impact and replace generic municipality-centre proximity.
corrections.validation: Conservative interim: when no selected breach/outer-dike footprint is supplied, direct flood extent, affected population and duration must be unknown/withheld rather than a centre-distance estimate; retain separately named synthetic exercise input if the user intentionally selects it. Durable public machine source: LIWO GeoServer OWS https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/geoserver/ows and catalogue API https://basisinformatie-overstromingen.nl/api/v2 provide named/versioned national scenario rasters for depth, arrival and duration. LIWO is release/layer-versioned rather than fixed-cadence, and its public portal did not expose a blanket redistribution licence during this audit; store layer/scenario/version/retrieval and clear terms before caching. Add Waterschapshuis Keringen IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-keringen-imwa/ogc/v1 (national barrier vectors, CC0; current landing has no fixed updateFrequency) and Oppervlaktewateren IMWA https://api.pdok.nl/hwh/waterschappen-oppervlaktewateren-imwa/ogc/v1 (water-system vectors, CC0; contributor coverage/freshness metadata required) only for mechanism/context—not to infer inundation from a line. Tests must distinguish named breach compartments, the small outer-dike strip and no-data, verify direct impact only inside a connected approved footprint, and rerun focused/national gates.

corrections.summary: Replace seeded Barendrecht water allocation with versioned local stress-test, terrain and drainage/catchment evidence.
corrections.validation: Request the municipality's machine export behind its official climate atlas/stress tests (the former bar.klimaatatlas.net currently redirects to https://bar.klimaatmonitor.net/); no stable public API, explicit reuse licence, raster resolution or refresh cadence was verified, so do not scrape or digitize the policy PDF. Integration-ready public covariates are AHN WCS https://service.pdok.nl/rws/actueel-hoogtebestand-nederland/wcs/v1_0?SERVICE=WCS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities (Rijkswaterstaat/PDOK DTM/DSM, 0.5 m products, cyclical edition, CC0), GWSW OGC API https://api.pdok.nl/rioned/waterschappen-waterketen-gwsw/ogc/v1 (sewer-context objects, CC0, landing cadence unspecified) and E08 IMWA/DAMO objects (object-level, CC BY-SA 4.0, completeness/cadence caveats). Define source-specific footprint metadata: mechanism, units, resolution, version, temporal validity, no-data, uncertainty and licence. Tests must make E04's source cells/hotspots—not a hash—govern local pluvial rank, allow different river/coastal/pluvial ordering, and prove that terrain or asset proximity alone is never presented as calibrated depth or failure.

corrections.summary: Add provider-aware public context and dated mobility inputs while leaving sensitive/unknown operational topology synthetic and explicit.

residualLimitations: The simulator is a deterministic planning stress test, not a KNMI forecast, warning, probability estimate, live incident picture, casualty model or operator outage forecast.
No approved Barendrecht LIWO/water-board breach, defence-state, depth, arrival, duration or compartment layer is ingested; normalized inundation stress is not measured metres.
Withholding unsupported generic direct water must not erase real primary/regional barrier, outer-dike, Oude Maas, pluvial, groundwater or sewer-overload mechanisms.
The municipal climate strategy and urban-water programme are authoritative policy/inventory sources but not reusable live machine topology, telemetry or calibrated operational forecasts.

CBS neighbourhoods and deterministic seeds do not resolve parcels, buildings, terrain depressions, cellars, dikes, drainage catchments, sewers, pumps, households, workers, visitors or individual vulnerability.
The public Waterschapshuis layer is intentionally partial; 118 intersecting objects cannot be reconciled as a complete inventory against differently scoped municipal sewer assets.
Barendrecht's Stedin context is absent from the current Liander-only overlay; static public geometry would still not provide operational connectivity, switching, capacity, state or restoration.

No physical drinking-water, sewer, electricity, gas, telecom, care or emergency-supply topology, live state, backup, priority-customer list, crew, fuel, spare or restoration estimate is available to the model.
All eight intermunicipal service layers reuse NWB-derived logical corridors and cannot be interpreted as cables, pipes, pressure zones, radio backhaul, patient transfers or food routes.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS inputs do not establish current closures, rail/timetable operation, vehicles, congestion, evacuation throughput or repair access.
Facilities and supply lack verified care roles, beds, staff, acceptance, care-home occupancy, pharmacies, supermarket/warehouse stock, depots, vehicles and continuity agreements.

Industrial and hazardous-material risk is regionally relevant but the canonical suite has no named Barendrecht facility/release scenario, plume model, substance, inventory or emergency response state.

Wildfire lacks a local incident perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind-aware spread, smoke dispersion, access and suppression state; earthquake lacks event probability, local ground motion, site response and asset fragility.
Generic preparedness, demand, backup, network, repair and intervention multipliers are transparent scenario controls rather than observed Barendrecht resources or commitments.

Six-hour checkpoints can miss cloudbursts, dispatch, traffic restrictions and schedule transitions; the 72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, contamination, public health, economic loss and reconstruction.
Rounded/suppressed CBS values and distinct CBS/BAG/BRT editions prevent false exact reconciliation across geographic products.
provinceReviewFlags: Review every Zuid-Holland municipality receiving river/coastal stress from shared centre-distance functions against a selected LIWO mechanism, defence/compartment state and connected footprint; do not equate administrative proximity with inundation.

Across IJsselmonde and Rotterdam-Rijnmond, distinguish outer-dike exposure, primary-barrier breach, regional-barrier failure, river high water, storm surge, pluvial overload, groundwater and sewer mechanisms before allocating neighbourhood impact.

Replace deterministic neighbourhood water ranks with coordinated LIWO, AHN, IMWA/GWSW and licensed municipal stress-test layers while retaining source resolution, version, no-data, licence and uncertainty.

Add provider-coverage semantics for Stedin, Liander and other operators so absence from one public dataset is never presented as absence of infrastructure; keep operational topology/state non-causal without authorization.

Coordinate Waterschapshuis, Stedin, RWS/PDOK, NDW, ProRail and CBS public context at province/operator scale, but never infer live state, sensitive topology, utility capacity, backup, stock, crews or restoration from static open data.
